cards.text: We're back at Shiloh, friend, with Eli the priest and his two sons. And the text doesn't even preheat the oven: it says the sons of Eli were wicked men, and they had no regard for the LORD.

cards.question: Eli's sons had no regard for the LORD, but they did respect the custom of the priests with the people.

cards.text: So here's what they do. When any man offers a sacrifice, the priest's servant comes over while the meat is still boiling, and he's carrying something.

cards.question: What does the priest's servant bring over to the boiling sacrifice?

cards.text: He plunges that fork into the pan or kettle or cauldron or cooking pot. This man is NOT picky, friend. If it's boiling, he's in it.

cards.question: Whatever the meat fork brings up out of the pot, the priest claims it for ___.
The fork in the pot only happens to a few of the Israelites who come to Shiloh.

cards.text: It gets worse. Even before the fat is burned, the servant walks up to the man sacrificing with a demand, like somebody reaching into my oven before the timer even goes off.

cards.question: Before the fat is burned, the servant says the priest wants meat to roast, and he'll only take it ___.

cards.text: And if a man pushes back and says burn the fat first, then take whatever you want, that sounds fair, right? You'd THINK so.

cards.question: If a man says to burn the fat first, how does the servant answer him?

answers.text: Give it now or I take it by force
Fine but the priest wants extra
Then the priest will take none

cards.question: The LORD sees the sin of Eli's sons as severe.
Eli's sons were treating the LORD's offering with ___.

cards.text: Now step away from all that grabbing and take a breath, friend. Samuel, the boy Hannah dedicated to the LORD (1 Samuel 1:28), is ministering before the LORD, wearing a linen ephod.
Each year his mother Hannah comes up with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice. And she brings Samuel something she made for him.

cards.question: What does Hannah make for Samuel and bring to him each year?

cards.text: And each year Eli blesses Elkanah and Hannah. He says may the LORD give them children by Hannah in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD.

cards.question: The LORD attends to Hannah after Eli's blessing. How many more children does she have?

cards.text: Five more children. FIVE. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.
Now Eli is very old, and he hears about everything his sons are doing to all Israel. He even hears that they're sleeping with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: Eli confronts his sons about everything he's heard. What does he ask them?

answers.text: Why are you doing these things
Who told you this was allowed
How long has this gone on

cards.text: He says he hears about their wicked deeds from all these people, and it's not a good report going around among the LORD's people. Friend, when the whole group chat is talking about you, it's never good news.

cards.question: Eli warns his sons that when a man sins against another man, God can intercede for him. What does Eli ask about a man who sins against the LORD?

answers.text: How will he pay it back

cards.question: Eli's sons take their father's warning to heart and listen to him.

cards.text: And the text tells us why they wouldn't listen: the LORD intended to put them to death. That's a heavy line, friend.

cards.question: Meanwhile, the boy Samuel keeps growing in stature. How else is he growing?

answers.text: In favor with the LORD and with man
In trouble with Eli and his sons
In charge of the priests' servants

cards.text: Then a man of God comes to Eli with a word from the LORD, and friend, this is NOT a social call. The LORD reminds Eli that He clearly revealed Himself to Eli's father's house back when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh's house.

cards.question: Out of all the tribes of Israel, the LORD selected Eli's father to be His ___.

cards.text: The LORD gave Eli's father's house ALL the food offerings of the Israelites, the whole cookie jar. So He asks Eli why he kicks at the sacrifice and offering He prescribed for His dwelling place.

cards.question: The LORD tells Eli that he has honored his ___ more than Him.

cards.text: And Eli doesn't get to stand off to the side: the LORD says Eli and his sons have been fattening themselves on the best of all the offerings of His people Israel. Friend, I've been caught with chocolate chips in my mustache, but this is a whole other level.
The LORD had said Eli's house would walk before Him FOREVER, friend. And now He declares, "Far be it from Me!"

cards.question: The LORD says He will honor those who honor Him, but He will overlook those who despise Him.

cards.text: Then the LORD gets to the hard part, and there's no sugar on it. No one in Eli's house will reach old age, and all his descendants will die by the sword of men.

cards.question: The LORD gives Eli a sign about his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. What is it?

answers.text: They will both die on the same day
They will both be sent far away
They will both be stripped of rank

cards.text: But then, friend, the message turns. The LORD will raise up a faithful priest for Himself, build him an enduring house, and that priest will walk before the LORD's anointed one for all time.

cards.question: The LORD says this faithful priest will do whatever is in the LORD's heart and mind.
Everyone left in Eli's house will come bow down to that faithful priest and plead to be appointed to some ___ office.

cards.text: The house that fattened itself on the best offerings will end up bowing for a piece of silver or a morsel of bread, begging for an office just to eat. We're stopping right there, friend, but this oven is still on.

findings.problem: The earlier cards rule out the wrong answers. Stop 2 card 6 says the LORD intended to put the sons to death (2:25). Card 15 says all of Eli's descendants will die by the sword of men (2:33). The question then asks for the sign about the two sons, and only the right answer, 'They will both die on the same day', involves death. The wrong answers 'sent far away' and 'stripped of rank' are already ruled out, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 Samuel 2:12, but it also uses Shiloh (2:14, or 1:3 from the earlier passage) and Eli's 'two sons' (2:34, or 1:3). These are facts from outside the cited verse, and the card gives no reference for them.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
